rule: No verification field is, by itself, permission to execute (Directive 010). `valid`, `verified`, `accepted`, `quorum_met`, `official`, `claim_verified` and similar are preconditions; success exits and HTTP 2xx require the explicit `authorized` decision (aml-authorization-decision/1) or are listed in REVIEWED_NON_AUTHORIZATION_SINKS / REVIEWED_DIAGNOSTIC_EXITS in the checker with a reason.
method: Enumeration by scripts/check-valid-field-decisions.mjs of every `.valid`, `?.valid`, ["valid"], .get("valid") read and `{ valid } =` destructuring in shipped JS/MJS/CJS/HTML/Python, positive valid-only sinks under test/, and every exit-0 / HTTP-2xx decision sink in JS/Python/Go. Valid-derived aliases (variables, destructuring, helper return values, object properties, imported helpers; Python via its AST) are rewritten to reads before sinks are matched, and their uses are listed. Directive 010 adds a rule that fails any shipped exit/HTTP success sink gated only on verification fields, and committed CodeQL data-flow queries (tooling/codeql/) that follow call arguments, containers, computed property names, multi-line expressions, imports and Go aliases. The lexical checker itself still does not follow call arguments, containers or dynamic property names; see docs/COMMAND_AUTHORIZATION.md.
